Prepare and load the resting heart rate data for my PVJ. I exported the data from my phone, and it’s only available as an xml. file. Online tools cannot successfully convert xml. to csv.
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(xml2)

# Path to apple health xml
file_path <- "pvj/apple_health_export/export.xml"
```

# AI Assistance to translate xml file into csv:

```{r}
file_path <- path.expand(
  "~/Documents/GitHub/ds112-portfolio-angelyan9966/pvj/apple_health_export/export.xml"
)

# Open the XML file for reading
con <- file(file_path, open = "r")

rhr_lines <- character()

repeat {
  lines <- readLines(con, n = 10000, warn = FALSE)

  if (length(lines) == 0) break

  matches <- grep(
    'type="HKQuantityTypeIdentifierRestingHeartRate"',
    lines,
    value = TRUE,
    fixed = TRUE
  )

  rhr_lines <- c(rhr_lines, matches)
}

close(con)

# Check the number of records
length(rhr_lines)

# Extract attributes from the XML records
extract_attr <- function(lines, attribute) {
  pattern <- paste0('.* ', attribute, '="([^"]*)".*')

  ifelse(
    grepl(paste0(' ', attribute, '="'), lines),
    sub(pattern, "\\1", lines),
    NA_character_
  )
}

rhr <- tibble(
  date = extract_attr(rhr_lines, "startDate"),
  resting_hr = as.numeric(extract_attr(rhr_lines, "value")),
  unit = extract_attr(rhr_lines, "unit")
)

# Explore the extracted data
head(rhr)
glimpse(rhr)
summary(rhr)

# Date conversion
rhr <- rhr %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(substr(date, 1, 10)))

# Save the extracted data locally
write_csv(rhr, file.path(dirname(file_path), "..",
                         "resting_heart_rate.csv"))
```

# my work start here

::: {.intro}
## My Resting Heart Rate (2025–2026)
For my PVJ I chose to explore my resting heart rate (rhr), by using data collected by my apple health. rhr is the number of times the heart beats per minute while the body is at rest. it can be influced at different factors. This project I will focus on the time in 2025 - 2026, especially as my daily routine shifts between academic semester, summer intern, and breaks. I hope to explore some noticeable patterns over time and how they might be impacted.
:::

```{r}
# Load data
rhr <- read_csv("pvj/resting_heart_rate.csv")

# Filter data from 2025 to 2026
rhr <- rhr |>
  filter(date >= as.Date("2025-01-01"), date <= as.Date("2026-10-28"))

# Explore the dataset
glimpse(rhr)
summary(rhr)
nrow(rhr)
```

```{r}
# Create by year and month
rhr <- rhr |>
  mutate(year = year(date), month = month(date))
```

```{r}
# Summarize rhr by year first
rhr_yearly <- rhr |>
  group_by(year) |>
   summarize(mean_rhr = mean(resting_hr))
rhr_yearly
```

```{r}
# viz: Resting Heart Rate Over Time
ggplot(rhr, aes(x = date, y = resting_hr, color = year)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 2) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.3) +
  labs(
    title = "how has my resting heart rate (rhr) changed?",
    subtitle = "rhs from 2025 to 2026",
    x = "date",
    y = "rhr (bpm)",
    caption = "export by Apple Health, January 2025 - October 2026"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# convert dates in academic calendar
academic_calendar <- academic_calendar |>
  mutate(start = mdy(start), end = mdy(end))
```

```{r}
# four academic semesters

# Spring 2025
spring_2025 <- rhr |>
  filter(date >= as.Date("2025-01-23"),
         date <= as.Date("2025-05-12")) |>
  summarize(mean_rhr = mean(resting_hr))

# Fall 2025
fall_2025 <- rhr |>
  filter(date >= as.Date("2025-09-02"),
         date <= as.Date("2025-12-17")) |>
  summarize(mean_rhr = mean(resting_hr))

# Spring 2026
spring_2026 <- rhr |>
  filter(date >= as.Date("2026-01-22"),
         date <= as.Date("2026-05-11")) |>
  summarize(mean_rhr = mean(resting_hr))

# Fall 2026
fall_2026 <- rhr |>
  filter(date >= as.Date("2026-09-08"),
         date <= as.Date("2026-10-28")) |>
  summarize(mean_rhr = mean(resting_hr))
```

```{r}
# average mean for four semester
spring_2025
fall_2025
spring_2026
fall_2026
```

```{r}
# filter academic semesters
rhr_semester <- rhr |>
  mutate(
    spring_2025 = date >= as.Date("2025-01-23") & date <= as.Date("2025-05-12"),
    fall_2025 = date >= as.Date("2025-09-02") & date <= as.Date("2025-12-17"),
    spring_2026 = date >= as.Date("2026-01-22") & date <= as.Date("2026-05-11"),
    fall_2026 = date >= as.Date("2026-09-08") & date <= as.Date("2026-10-28")
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(spring_2025, fall_2025, spring_2026, fall_2026),
    names_to = "semester",
    values_to = "included"
  ) |>
  filter(included == TRUE)

# average rhr by year and academic period
rhr_semester_avg <- rhr_semester |>
  group_by(semester) |>
  summarize(mean_rhr = mean(resting_hr))
rhr_semester_avg                            
```

```{r}
# viz: rhr across these four academic periods
ggplot(rhr_semester_avg, aes(x = semester, y = mean_rhr, color = semester)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "my rhr across four academic semesters",
    subtitle = "average rhr in spring and fall, 2025–2026",
    x = "semester",
    y = "average rhr (bpm)",
    color = "semester",
    caption = "source: Apple Health & Macalester Calendar"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

::: {.callout-note title = "observations"}
My average rhr was lower in 2026 than in 2025 for both Spring and Fall. In both years, my rhr was also slightly higher in Spring than in Fall. The difference between the four groups was relatively small, but the pattern was at least consistent across the two years.

my originally thought is wanted to see whether my heart rate changes with my academic schedule. However, these results do not necessarily mean that academic stress caused the differences, since RHR can also be affected by sleep, exercise, emotions, and other factors.
:::
